entry.summary: No visa for tourism. With a chipped passport, e-gates at major airports authorise up to 180 days for tourism only.
entry.max_stay: Up to 180 days, but the officer sets the date: check the stamp or e-gate QR record.
entry.pre_arrival: Without e-gates: the online Multiple Immigration Form (FMM) and a QR code, shown on departure too. By land, get the passport stamped at the nearest immigration office and pay the fee.
entry.other: E-gates are for tourism only, adults only, and not when travelling with minors.

laws.rule: Anyone entering or leaving Mexico with more than US$10,000 (or the equivalent in other currencies) in cash, cheques or similar must declare it. Carrying it is not a crime; not declaring it is penalised. US$10,000 is about A$14,200 (RBA 30 Oct 2026: A$1 = USD 0.7040).
laws.penalty_signal: Fine of 20% to 40% of the amount over US$10,000; if the undeclared amount is over US$30,000, 3 months to 6 years in prison and the excess goes to the federal treasury unless its lawful origin is shown

laws.rule: Duty-free baggage allowance for passengers over 18: up to 3 litres of alcoholic drinks and 6 litres of wine. Goods beyond baggage worth up to US$500 (about A$710) in total can come in under the separate franchise, which cannot include tobacco products.

Duty-free tobacco for passengers over 18: up to 20 packs of cigarettes, 25 cigars or 200 grams of tobacco. Electronic cigarettes and similar vaping devices, including heated-tobacco and nicotine-free systems, are on ANAM's list of goods that cannot be brought into Mexico.
laws.penalty_signal: Goods that cannot be imported can be seized by Customs

laws.rule: Medicines for personal use may come in as part of baggage, along with blood-pressure and glucose meters. For psychotropic substances (medicines acting on the mind, such as some sleep, anxiety or ADHD medicines) the doctor's prescription must be shown.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: No visa for tourism. With a chipped ordinary passport, adults can use the e-gates at major airports for tourism stays of up to 180 days; otherwise a visa on arrival is given at the border, for the length the immigration officer sets (up to 180 days, not guaranteed). Complete the online Multiple Immigration Form (FMM) and make sure the passport is stamped.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: e-gates at major airports for adults with a chipped ordinary passport travelling for tourism only (up to 180 days, QR code printed).
visa-preparation.before_departure: Fill in the FMM online (or on arrival) and keep the QR code. If routing through the US or Canada, meet their transit rules (an eTA for Canada). Entering by road, find the immigration office near the border for the stamp.
visa-preparation.useful_stay: Up to 180 days for tourism, set by the officer or e-gate; business, study or work need other visas.

steps.step: Complete the Multiple Immigration Form (FMM) online before arrival, or on arrival, and keep the QR code.
At major airports, use the e-gates if eligible (chipped ordinary passport, 18 or over, tourism only, no minors); download the e-tourist card within 60 days.
Otherwise, check the date stamped on arrival: it sets the stay.
By road, get the passport stamped at the INM office near the crossing and pay the immigration fee at a nearby bank.
Declare goods over the duty-free allowance and keep receipts for high-value items.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: NOM-107-SCT3-2019 sets RPAS rules: registration with the Registro Aeronautico Mexicano and an operating authorisation for commercial use. As summarised, it says foreign-registered RPAS and foreign operators cannot operate in Mexico unless a bilateral agreement exists with the state of registry.

items.text: Not yet checked: no public AFAC directory of RPAS operators was found on the pages read.

RPAS are registered in the Registro Aeronautico Mexicano before operating (start with Apendice K and rpas@afac.gob.mx). The norm defines commercial use as operation for profit and requires registration and an operating authorisation for small RPAS.

As summarised from NOM-107-SCT3-2019, RPAS with foreign registration and foreign operators cannot operate in Mexico unless a bilateral agreement exists between Mexico's aeronautical authority and the civil aviation authority of the state of registry. AFAC's aerial survey instructions ask foreign applicants for a current foreign pilot licence and documents showing legal stay. Confirm with AFAC (rpas@afac.gob.mx).
